newsitem.title: CHINA: Gore says too early to judge China on fund raising.
newsitem.headline: Gore says too early to judge China on fund raising.

text.p: U.S. Vice President Al Gore has told China there would be no immediate change in U.S. policy following allegations Beijing made illegal payments to the U.S. Democratic party, a senior U.S. official said on Wednesday.
"It is premature to say that an investigation that hasn't been completed yet is going to have a major impact on the relationship," said the senior official who declined to be identified.

"If the allegations are later proven to be true then they are very serious and we'll deal with it at that time," said the official who took part in talks on Tuesday between Gore and Chinese Premier Li Peng.
"The controversy by itself without facts being established does not have an impact on the relationship and should not," he said.
China's Li had raised the controversy in Tuesday's talks and "vigorously denied" that Beijing had sent funds into campaign coffers of Democratic Party candidates in the 1996 elections.
The fund-raising uproar is particularly sensitive for Gore, because he and U.S. President Bill Clinton have been accused of questionable fundraising practices in their re-election campaign.
